newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale plans grain-rail meet on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale plans grain-rail meet on Thursday.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale will broker a meeting between the grain and rail transportation industries in Calgary Thursday evening in the hopes of finding a way out of the current grain shipment impasse, Goodale's spokesman told Reuters.

"He's going to hold a meeting Thursday night in Calgary. He (Goodale) decided this afternoon that he had enough of them lined up that he'd have a meeting to get the grain moving again," Goodale spokesman Vern Greenshields said.
There were 42 ships waiting to load grains and oilseeds at Pacific ports on Monday, 37 for Canadian Wheat Board grains.
A dozen ships waiting to load were destined for Japan. The longest waiting ship had been in port 39 days, the CWB said.
Heavy snow, the cold and sporadic Prairie elevator grain deliveries were blamed by the railways for the delay.
The CWB along with some grain and transportation analysts said grain shipments were a lower priority for the railways since they generate lower profits versus other commodities.
The CWB last week estimated the cost of lost or deferred grain sales and demurrage fines to have reached C$65 million.
Rail rates on grain cannot exceed a federally imposed cap while other commodities may get priority because of premiums.
The Canadian government is due to review the grain rail rate cap and perhaps its necessity in 1999.

The CWB, Canadian grain industry, Canadian National Railway Co and Canadian Pacific unit CP Rail System as well as Vancouver and Prince Rupert port officials were scheduled to attend the closed door meeting at an undisclosed Calgary location, Greenshields said.
The delay may lead importers to look elsewhere for grain.
Wheat and oats markets in the United States rallied Tuesday on news the CWB passed on sales for February and March delivery and that April sales were now threatened.
